messages:
anna-security: Heads-up: starting ~09:20 UTC we saw a spike in mTLS handshake failures for services in ap-south behind proxy-ephemeral. Metrics show increased TLS handshake timeouts and dropped connections. Also noticing cert-rotation audit events missing for that region. Anyone seeing this?

mike-sre: Yep, seeing 502s and a bunch of `tls: handshake error: EOF` in ingress logs. Quick check with openssl shows no cert chain presented from the service host.

mike-sre: ```
$ openssl s_client -connect svc-orders.ap-south.redwood.internal:443 -tls1_3 -servername svc-orders
CONNECTED(00000003)
140704123456320:error:1425F102:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:unsupported protocol:s3_lib.c:???
---
No peer certificate available
---
``` 

raj-crypto: My hunch: the ephemeral rotator rollout (v2) changed issuer chain to a CA that was encrypted with a different KMS key/alias. If the rotator SA lost kms:Decrypt on new key or the proxy cannot fetch intermediate chain from keystore, clients will fail. Also if the rotator wrote secrets without the `redwood.com/chain` annotation, proxies may skip serving chain.

dana-ops: I pulled the rotator logs in ap-south: `cert-rotator-v2` pod shows lots of `failed to unwrap key: AccessDeniedException` around 09:18-09:22 UTC. Example log line: `wrap: kms:Decrypt denied for key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:111222333:key/abcd-rotator`.

dana-ops: ```
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/cert-rotator-v2 | grep AccessDeniedException | tail -n 5
# shows repeated denies across multiple pods
```

auditbot: Checked audit logs: no `cert.rotate` events emitted for ap-south between 09:00-10:00 UTC. There are rotator retries but success events are absent. KMS API calls exist but show `AccessDenied` from KMS side.

anna-security: That fits. Two attack surfaces: RBAC change for rotator SA / role, and KMS key policy drift. @raj-crypto can you confirm key policy and recent IAM changes? @mike-sre can you confirm whether proxies are reloading certs when secret updates fail?

raj-crypto: On it. Quick check: `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id abcd-rotator --policy-name default` returns a policy that lists `arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/cert-rotator-role` in the principals — but I see an extra condition tied to `sts:SourceIdentity` that the new rotator deployment doesn't set. Looks like a deployment PR added a glue condition. TL;DR: the rotator process isn't assuming the expected identity -> KMS denies.

raj-crypto: Suggested mitigation:
- Revert rotator to v1 (which uses the older role mapping), or
- Patch KMS key policy to accept new SourceIdentity value used by rotator-v2.

mike-sre: Proxies will not reload partial secrets. If the secret update created a TLS secret without `tls.crt` (chain missing) the proxy returns 502 until a full, valid secret exists. Rolling back rotator to v1 should restore the previous secrets.

dana-ops: I can roll back the rotator deployment now and run a canary. Command I will use:
```
kubectl -n infra set image deploy/cert-rotator cert-rotator=ghcr.io/redwood/rotator:v1.14.2
kubectl -n infra rollout status deploy/cert-rotator
```
I'll also force proxies in ap-south to reload once secrets stabilized: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/proxy-ap-south` (canary first).

oncall: Taking this. I'll coordinate with infra and security. ETA to revert + canary: 18 min. Will post progress.

mike-sre: Also add temporary fallback: proxy routing rule to route traffic to eu fallback pool for critical routes while we observe. Quick nginx snippet to set upstream fallback for routes `orders`, `billing`.

anna-security: Can we capture forensic artifacts before we change anything? Need rotator pod logs, KMS CloudTrail entries, and the failing secret YAMLs. @dana-ops please archive to s3://redwood-incident-ap-south/1755001234 and snapshot KMS entries.

dana-ops: Copy. Will upload tarball of `/var/log/rotator/*` logs and `kubectl get secret svc-orders -n prod -o yaml` to that S3 path.

raj-crypto: Post-mortem note: we should avoid adding `SourceIdentity` dependent policy for core rotator keys; prefer explicit role ARNs or resource-based policies that allow both v1 and v2 identities. I'll open a policy-change PR after containment.

auditbot: Audit entries created: `s3://redwood-incident-ap-south/1755001234/logs.tgz` and `cloudtrail` snapshot `ct-ap-south-1755001234.json`.

oncall: Revert applied at 09:40 UTC, rolling canary shows success. Proxies restarted. Early metrics show handshake failure rate back down to baseline.

mike-sre: Verified `openssl s_client` now shows full chain and certificate:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect svc-orders.ap-south.redwood.internal:443 -servername svc-orders
CONNECTED(...)
depth=2 CN = Redwood Ephemeral CA
verify return:1
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

anna-security: Good. For follow-up actions:
- raj-crypto: PR to KMS policy + add automated key policy tests in CI (ticket #INC-1755)
- dana-ops: runbook update: include KMS policy verification steps and `kubectl get secret` checks (ticket #INC-1756)
- mike-sre: add proxy health check that alerts on missing chain vs. certificate validity (ticket #INC-1757)
- infra: add canary gating for rotator rollouts tied to successful KMS decrypts (ticket #INC-1758)

dana-ops: I updated runbook draft: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/mtls-rotation (added the KMS checklist)

raj-crypto: Opening PRs now. I'll add a test in our infra-qa that simulates KMS deny to catch this during rollout.

anna-security: Closing thread: rotator rolled back, audit artifacts archived, follow-up tickets created. Thanks all :thumbsup:

oncall: Marking incident resolved in pager duty and creating follow-up timeline in the postmortem doc.
